The Fastify version string is defined in **`package.json`, line 3**:

```json
"version": "2.3.0"
```

This is the root `package.json` at `/Users/admin/Projects/sweet-search-private/package.json`, which also declares `"name": "fastify"` on line 2 — confirming this is the Fastify package's own version definition.

The `applicationHooks` array is defined at **lines 3–10** of `lib/hooks.js` and contains 6 hooks:

| Hook | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `onRoute` | Fired when a new route is registered |
| `onRegister` | Fired when a new plugin is registered |
| `onReady` | Fired after all plugins are loaded, before the server starts listening |
| `onListen` | Fired after the server starts listening |
| `preClose` | Fired before the server begins its shutdown sequence |
| `onClose` | Fired when the server is closing |

These are distinct from the **lifecycle hooks** (lines 11–22), which are per-request hooks like `onRequest`, `preParsing`, `preValidation`, etc. The full combined set is exported as `supportedHooks = lifecycleHooks.concat(applicationHooks)` (line 23).

Notably, in `buildHooks()` (lines 73–91), `onReady`, `onListen`, and `preClose` are always reset to `[]` on child scope creation — they are not inherited across plugin scopes, unlike the other application hooks.

Fastify registers exactly **two** default content-type parsers, defined in `lib/content-type-parser.js` lines 37–39:

| Content-Type | Parser | `parseAs` |
|---|---|---|
| `application/json` | `defaultJsonParser` (via `secure-json-parse`) | `string` |
| `text/plain` | `defaultPlainTextParser` (returns body as-is) | `string` |

**Details from the source:**

```js
// lib/content-type-parser.js, lines 33–41
function ContentTypeParser (bodyLimit, onProtoPoisoning, onConstructorPoisoning) {
  this[kDefaultJsonParse] = getDefaultJsonParser(onProtoPoisoning, onConstructorPoisoning)
  this.customParsers = new Map()
  this.customParsers.set('application/json', new Parser(true, false, bodyLimit, this[kDefaultJsonParse]))
  this.customParsers.set('text/plain',       new Parser(true, false, bodyLimit, defaultPlainTextParser))
  this.parserList = ['application/json', 'text/plain']
```

- **`application/json`** — reads the full body as a UTF-8 string, then calls `secureJsonParse` (proto/constructor poisoning protection configurable via `onProtoPoisoning`/`onConstructorPoisoning` options). Throws `FST_ERR_CTP_EMPTY_JSON_BODY` on empty body, `FST_ERR_CTP_INVALID_JSON_BODY` on parse failure (lines 311–321).
- **`text/plain`** — reads the full body as a UTF-8 string and passes it through unchanged (`done(null, body)`, line 325).

Any other content-type (e.g. `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, `multipart/form-data`) will result in a `415 Unsupported Media Type` error unless you register a custom parser via `fastify.addContentTypeParser(...)`. You can also register `'*'` as a catch-all wildcard parser.
